title: Centre Shares Timelines For Key Flyovers And Elevated Corridor Projects In Pune
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Dec 04, 2025, 10:06 AM | Updated 10:06 AM IST

The Centre has released a status update on a series of critical highway development works across the Pune Metropolitan Region, highlighting progress on new flyovers, elevated corridors and major road-widening efforts.
In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari outlined project timelines and ongoing interventions designed to ease persistent traffic bottlenecks and improve long-term connectivity on key National Highways.
According to the ministry, four significant interventions had been sanctioned to address chronic traffic bottlenecks. The integrated structures at Chandani Chowk on NH-48 were completed in March 2024, marking the first of the projects to be delivered.
The six-lane flyover at Katraj Junction on NH-548DD is targeted for completion in June 2026, while the concreting of service and slip roads along the 41 km Pune–Satara stretch of NH-48 is expected to finish by June 2027.
The longest project, elevated corridors between Nashik Phata and Khed on NH-60, covering 30 km has a planned completion date of March 2030.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has also begun feasibility studies for an elevated corridor between Ravet and Narhe on NH-48, signalling further expansion of high-capacity routes around Pune.
In parallel, an MoU has been signed with the Maharashtra State Infrastructure Development Corporation (MSIDC) for proposed elevated corridors or capacity upgrades on three additional stretches: Pune–Shirur (NH-753F), Talegaon–Chakan–Shikrapur (NH-548D) and Hadapsar–Yavat (NH-65). These will proceed based on technical assessments.
To ensure timely progress, the ministry noted that regular coordination meetings are being held between NHAI, the Pune Municipal Corporation, the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority and other state and central agencies to resolve pending issues and speed up project execution.
